title: Affine tensor unit section presentation by diagonal-action relations
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-pc-scheme]. Write $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_U$, let $\rho:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal A$ be the structure map, and let $r_0:f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_U$, $t_0=f^{-1}\rho$, and $e:f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal O_U$ be the structure map, inverse-image map, and ring inverse-image/direct-image counit. Write $R$ for pushforward as an $\mathcal A$-module, and $S$ for restriction to $\mathcal O_X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Tensor pullback and change of rings are those of [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and the adjunction is the canonical one of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Let $B$ be a commutative ring sheaf on $U$, with $b:\mathcal O_U\to B$, $t:f^{-1}\mathcal A\to B$, and $\epsilon:B\to\mathcal O_U$, where the square $(r_0,t_0,b,t)$ is a pushout, $b\epsilon=1$, and $t\epsilon=e$. Let $P:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ be change of rings along $t$ after inverse image on objects and morphisms. Let $\kappa:P\operatorname{res}_b\simeq Sf^*$ carry the pullback unit, after inversion and the object equality, to $1\otimes\eta(n)$. Let $H:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_U)$ be change of rings along $\epsilon$ after $P$, on objects and morphisms, and let $\gamma:Sf^*\to H$ satisfy the section formula $\gamma\kappa(p)=1\otimes p$ after the object equality and sheafification; assume $H$ preserves quasi-coherence. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-module $G$ and affine open $V\subseteq X$, put $D=\mathcal O_X(V)$, $C=\mathcal O_U(f^{-1}V)$, and $N=G(V)$, with its given $C=\mathcal A(V)$-action and restricted $D$-action. There exists a surjective $D$-linear map $q:C\otimes_D N\to H(G)(f^{-1}V)$ whose kernel is the $D$-span of $c\otimes n-1\otimes(cn)$ for $c\in C,n\in N$, and such that $q(1\otimes n)=\gamma_{G,f^{-1}V}(\mathrm{unit}_{SG,V}(n))$.

proof.text: Apply the affine pushout first-tensor section comparison to obtain delta and p with the two actions, additive generation and normalized unit formula. These data concern B and P only, before extension along epsilon.

The existing affine pushout-algebra theorem makes B quasi-coherent. Pushforward of the structure-sheaf unit gives quasi-coherence of A; scalar restriction makes SG quasi-coherent. Compare tensorPullback with the ordinary module pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints and transfer pullback quasi-coherence through kappa to the underlying P(G). For the O_U-algebra map epsilon:(B,b)->(O_U,1), the affine change-of-rings theorem gives a bijective sheafification map on W. Transport its additive equivalence through hobj to obtain e:C tensor_E M -> H(G)(W).

Define q=gamma_W kappa_W p; it is D-linear. The hH formula identifies q(z)=e(1 tensor p(z)). In the proved private scalar_tensor_presentation, define a(c tensor n)=cn and tau=a p inverse. The two action formulas give tau(b(c)m)=c tau(m) and tau(delta(c)m)=c tau(m); finite additive generation makes tau epsilon-balanced for all E-scalars. Thus c tensor m maps additively to c tau(m) in N, showing ker(q) is contained in ker(a). Delta-balancing kills each c tensor n - 1 tensor cn. Tensor induction shows z - 1 tensor a(z) belongs to their D-span, so ker(q) is exactly that span. Balancing with b(c) rewrites c tensor p(z)=1 tensor p(c z), making q surjective by double tensor induction. This is a complete Lean proof using TensorProduct.liftAddHom and Submodule.span_le, with no new algebraic hole.

The unit formula for p and kappa hom-inv imply q(1 tensor n)=gamma_W(unit(n)). No beta and no adjoint comparison are used. All constructions work with zero modules, zero rings and the empty affine open.
